the-age-of-electric.bio:
The Age of Electric emerged from Saskatchewan at the turn of the 1990s, built around two pairs of brothers: Todd and John Kerns and Ryan and Kurt Dahle. Years of playing Western Canadian clubs gave the group a tight, high-energy foundation before the independently released Ugly EP began attracting national attention. The band then moved to Mercury Records, bringing a Prairie-rooted alternative-rock act into the major-label Canadian rock system at the height of the 1990s guitar boom.

The 1997 album Make a Pest a Pet became the group's defining full-length statement. Its lead single, "Remote Control," reached the Canadian Top 10, while the album was certified gold in Canada. Songs such as "I Don't Mind" and "Don't Wreck It" reinforced the band's combination of distorted guitars, melodic hooks and restless arrangements. The record arrived just as its members' parallel projects were becoming increasingly important, and The Age of Electric's original run ended not long after.

The band's significance extends well beyond its relatively compact catalogue. Ryan and Kurt Dahle had already formed Limblifter, which became a major outlet for Ryan's songwriting, while Kurt later joined The New Pornographers and Todd Kerns built a long international career that eventually included work with Slash. The Age of Electric reunited in the 2010s and revisited Make a Pest a Pet for its 20th anniversary, underscoring how the band functions as a connective point in Canadian rock: a Saskatchewan act whose members fed directly into several important strands of the country's later alternative and power-pop history.
the-age-of-electric.directory_summary: Saskatchewan's The Age of Electric turned years of Western Canadian club work into a national alternative-rock breakthrough. The gold-certified Make a Pest a Pet and Top 10 single "Remote Control" became 1990s Canadian rock staples, while members Ryan and Kurt Dahle and Todd Kerns went on to major roles in Limblifter, The New Pornographers and other projects, giving the band's compact catalogue an unusually large afterlife.

limblifter.bio:
Limblifter began in Vancouver in the mid-1990s as a side project for The Age of Electric brothers Ryan and Kurt Dahle with bassist Ian Somers, but quickly developed an identity of its own. The self-titled debut produced Canadian alternative-radio staples including "Tinfoil," "Vicious" and "Screwed It Up," establishing Ryan Dahle's combination of crooked guitar textures, melodic power pop and idiosyncratic songwriting as the band's centre of gravity. When The Age of Electric ended, Limblifter became his primary long-term vehicle.

The 2000 album Bellaclava deepened that approach with songs such as "Ariel vs. Lotus" and "Wake Up to the Sun." Lineup changes became part of the band's history: Kurt Dahle and Todd Fancey moved into The New Pornographers, while Ryan rebuilt Limblifter around new collaborators for I/O in 2004. Across those changes, the group accumulated five Top 11 Canadian radio hits and three JUNO nominations, giving it a durable place in the country's alternative-rock network even without the scale of a conventional arena-rock career.

Limblifter's later catalogue has made that continuity clearer. Pacific Milk arrived in 2015 and Little Payne in 2022, while the band returned to regular live activity with a lineup centred on Ryan Dahle and bassist Megan Bradfield and, more recently, drummer Jeremy Taggart of Our Lady Peace. The group's longevity also mirrors Dahle's wider role as a producer, collaborator and member of Mounties. Limblifter matters as more than a 1990s radio memory: it is one of the connective projects linking The Age of Electric, The New Pornographers and several generations of Vancouver and Canadian indie rock.
limblifter.directory_summary: Vancouver's Limblifter grew from an Age of Electric side project into Ryan Dahle's enduring alternative-rock vehicle. The self-titled debut, Bellaclava and radio songs including "Tinfoil" and "Ariel vs. Lotus" established the band's melodic but off-centre guitar sound. Its shifting membership also connects Limblifter directly to The New Pornographers, Mounties and other major threads in Canadian indie rock.
